bites.title: Under the hood
bites.body: Every material is secretly a little machine of nodes. Boxes do jobs, wires carry data from left to right, and the Material Output on the far right is the finish line.

bites.title: Find your way
bites.body: Hover the Shader Editor at the bottom. Scroll to zoom, middle-drag to pan, Home to fit everything on screen. Same moves as the viewport.

bites.title: Add a texture
bites.body: Hover the Shader Editor, press Shift+A, then Texture, then Noise Texture. Click to drop it.
bites.hint: Shift+A must be pressed with the mouse over the Shader Editor, not the viewport.

bites.title: Plug it in
bites.body: Drag from the Noise node's yellow Color dot to the Base Color dot on Principled BSDF. Your cube turns cloudy.
bites.hint: Yellow dots carry color. Drag dot to dot.

bites.title: Zoom the pattern
bites.body: On the Noise node, set Scale to 20. Finer grain.

bites.title: Splice in color
bites.body: Shift+A, Converter, Color Ramp. Drop it right ON the wire between Noise and Principled. Blender splices it in for you.
bites.hint: Drag the new node over the wire until the wire highlights, then click.

bites.title: Choose the palette
bites.body: Click the black stop on the Color Ramp, then click the color bar below it and pick a color. Do the white one too.

bites.title: Make it bumpy
bites.body: Shift+A, Vector, Bump. Wire Noise's Fac into Bump's Height, and Bump's Normal into Principled's Normal.
bites.hint: Two wires: Noise Fac to Bump Height, Bump Normal to Principled Normal (purple dots).

bites.title: Lesson 09: cleared
bites.body:
Adding nodes, wiring them, splicing, color ramps, and bump. That's the grammar of every procedural material.

Scroll on for Lesson 10: light.
